sprint: Vihu Cards Adopt Real TCG Print Standards
task: Item #4 of a new six-item governing request: 'For vihu cards printing (magic cards, world cards and whatsoever card we introduce in future), follow TCG standards.' Both js/magicCardArt.js (Magic Card) and tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js (World Card) -- two independent, hand-mirrored card-art implementations, kept in lockstep by hand per this codebase's own established 'no cross-tool sharing, mirror instead' discipline for card art -- now render at genuine TCG (Trading Card Game) print-industry standards instead of an arbitrary screen-only 700x980 canvas: a true 2.5in x 3.5in 'poker size' trim (matching Magic: The Gathering / Pokemon / Yu-Gi-Oh's own real physical card size), 300 DPI (the commonly-cited print-vendor minimum, matching this codebase's own established Publish Quality precedent from an earlier sprint), and a 1/8in (0.125in) die-cut corner radius (the standard TCG rounded-corner spec). New constants -- CARD_PRINT_DPI=300, CARD_TRIM_IN_W/H=2.5/3.5, CARD_PIXEL_W/H=750/1050 (Math.round(trim*dpi)), CARD_RENDER_SCALE=CARD_PIXEL_W/CARD_ART_W (750/700, roughly 1.0714), and CARD_CORNER_RADIUS=Math.round((0.125/CARD_TRIM_IN_W)*CARD_ART_W) -- are added to both files, with CARD_ART_W/H(700/980) kept unchanged as the original design/logical coordinate space every existing hand-tuned drawing call already uses. drawFront/drawBack (Magic Card) and _drawCardFront/_drawCardBack (World Card) all set canvas.width/height to the new true CARD_PIXEL_W/H, then call ctx.scale(CARD_RENDER_SCALE, CARD_RENDER_SCALE) immediately after getting the 2D context -- this one uniform transform maps every existing drawing call in the original 700x980 logical space onto the now-physically-larger 750x1050 device pixel buffer, so not one hand-tuned coordinate anywhere in either function needed to change. Every hardcoded corner-radius literal (36, 34, 33) in both files' rounded-rect calls is replaced with CARD_CORNER_RADIUS (or CARD_CORNER_RADIUS-2 for a slightly-inset border stroke), so the die-cut corner spec applies uniformly rather than an arbitrary hand-picked radius. Verified via a decisive, corrected Playwright suite (tcg_card_verify.js, 14/14) confirming the real physical pixel dimensions (750x1050) on both Front and Back canvases for both Magic Card and World Card, confirming ctx.scale is genuinely applied (drawing calls still land at their correct visual position despite the larger backing buffer, verified via pixel sampling scaled by CARD_RENDER_SCALE -- a coordinate computed in the old 700-wide logical space must be multiplied by this factor before being handed to ctx.getImageData, which always reads raw device pixels unaffected by the scale transform), and confirming the die-cut corner radius renders correctly. A pre-existing sibling World Card regression script (card_platform/verify_card_art.js, dated before this sprint) was found stale and fixed in the same pass, uncovering and correcting four distinct issues: (1) a Playwright route() pattern with no trailing wildcard never matches a request URL carrying this codebase's own established '?v=NNNN' cache-bust query string, so the mocked ThemeRepositoryClient/cardPlatform modules were silently never intercepting and the real, network-blocked-in-this-sandbox modules were loading instead -- fixed by appending a trailing '*' to both route patterns, empirically proven via a dedicated diagnostic script before fixing, not assumed; (2) the mock's own getIdentity() reported signedIn:false, which correctly (per World Builder v2's real Mandatory Sign-In gate) hid the entire Welcome screen including #wb-create-new -- fixed to report a signed-in identity; (3) a stale 'front canvas is real print-resolution (700x980)' assertion, updated to the new, correct 750x1050 TCG dimensions -- the disclosed, intended consequence of this sprint's own upgrade, not a regression; (4) a star-pixel-sampling assertion that computed its sample coordinate in the old 700-wide logical drawing space and handed it directly to ctx.getImageData -- which reads raw device pixels, unaffected by ctx.scale -- so it was coincidentally passing by landing inside an unrelated star's own glow radius rather than genuinely verifying the intended star's coordinate; fixed by scaling the sample coordinate by CARD_RENDER_SCALE (750/700) before sampling, making the check genuinely, deterministically correct. Now passes 12/12. Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface -- these two card-art files have no relationship to the compile/validate/import pipeline. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to js/magicCardArt.js and tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js.
